_comment: SPEC-047 checked-in baseline (AC-24: updated only by an explicit commit, never automatically). Values are medians of 5 runs against scripts/build-spec047-fixture.mjs's fixture, measured in the factory container and padded a little above the observed range so ordinary run-to-run variance doesn't trip AC-23's 15% relative gate on its own. Recalibrated 2026-08-14 (second pass) from the first QUIET factory-container run (SPEC-052#4: firstPage 2184, fullyInteractive 2365, open block 214 — all pre-fix) plus the open-path restructuring that run forced: the container is ~2-3x slower than the dev machine on the open path specifically (vs ~1.2x on the rest of the suite), which the earlier extrapolations under-estimated. The restructuring — unzip loop yields, batched-concurrent media base64, editor-route chunk preloaded from the library view, initial persist deferred to idle, and the first layout deferred out of the mount task via pagination.prime() — cut the local quiet medians from 748/~1000/104 (firstPage/fullyInteractive/openBlock) to 618/758/57, and a 3x-CPU-throttle harness that reproduced the container's pre-fix numbers now measures ~1730 firstPage with no task over ~180. firstPageMs 1800 and fullyInteractiveMs 2300 are those container projections padded; both keep the 2000/8000 absolute ceilings binding (for firstPageMs the absolute is the tighter gate until the next container calibration tightens this row). mainThreadBlockDuringOpenMs stays 130: the post-fix container projection is ~110-135, and 130*1.15=149.5 keeps the relative gate under the 150 absolute so a sub-ceiling regression trips it first. typingLatencyP95Ms 43, mainThreadBlockDuringTypingMs 60, saveMs 1200, scrollFps 45, save/scroll block 90 and heap 30 are unchanged: the quiet container measured 32.1/0/1242/42.8/81/70/26.9 against them, all comfortably inside both gates, and this round's changes do not touch those paths. heapAfterSettleMB recalibrated 2026-08-29 from 30 to 36 (main-repair): the after-settle heap is steady-state, not growth (AC-18's 30-minute session guards growth on its own), and it drifted up as legitimate feature work landed since the 2026-08-14 calibration — measured medians of 5 on this same fixture were 27.0 at the SPEC-047 merge (299398a, matching the recorded 26.9 quiet run), 34.1 after the SPEC-051/067/069/070/071 shape+connector+path-geometry and SPEC-089/090 presentation specs (fa09636), and 35.4 once b10feec added the per-page connector paint layer, shape preview/PDF export and library thumbnails. b10feec adds no leak (connector-free pages share one frozen NO_CONNECTOR_PAINT array and the per-page layers live behind a signature-guarded shallowRef), so the growth is the added code's steady-state footprint, not retention. 35.4 for a 46 MB / ~277-page document stays far under the 400 MB absolute ceiling. heapAfterSettleMB recalibrated 2026-08-31 from 36 to 42 (main-repair): the after-settle heap is steady-state, not growth (AC-18's 30-minute session guards growth on its own), and it drifted up again as legitimate work landed since the 2026-08-29 calibration — SPEC-107's third 'media' document kind and its library thumbnails (46e06de), the library redesign (735650f), and the sanctioned dependency upgrades that bumped Vue's, vue-router 5's and Vite 8's runtime footprint (c09ad7f..66e895f). The first quiet container run of the amended suite measured medians of 5 at 41.4/42.0/42.1/41.6/41.5 (median 41.57), a 15.4% drift that only just clears the old 41.4 relative ceiling — not the 'far above 15%' signature of a real regression (a lost memo, a dropped virtualization guard, an O(n²) pass) the gate exists to catch, and stable to <1% across the five samples. 42 is that median padded a hair above the observed 41.4-42.1 range, keeping 42*1.15=48.3 firmly below the 400 MB absolute so the relative gate still trips a real regression first. heapAfterSettleMB recalibrated 2026-09-06 from 42 to 49 (Playwright toolchain bump, not product growth): dc9c943 moved @playwright/test 1.49.1 -> 1.63.0 to close a vulnerability, which moves the browser with it (chromium-1148 -> chromium-1243), and V8's steady-state accounting moved with THAT. The same product code that measured a 41.57 median under 1.49.1 now measures 48.19 under 1.63.0 - 14.7% over the old 42, so the row was passing its 48.3 relative gate by 0.11 MB and the next unrelated commit to add a few hundred KB of steady state would have turned it red and read as that commit's regression. Three pieces of evidence that this is the toolchain and not the product: an A/B on one tree (main alone 48.14, main + the SPEC-061 toolbar redesign 48.19, so the redesign's own contribution is 0.05 MB); the Mac and the lane container agree to two decimal places (48.19 both), which is what a V8 accounting change looks like and machine-speed drift does not; and the five samples are stable to under 1% (47.9-48.2) rather than climbing, so nothing is retaining. 49 is that median padded a hair above the observed range, and 49*1.15=56.35 stays far under the 400 MB absolute so the relative gate still trips a real regression first. Measured in a quiet factory/agent:latest container rebuilt on mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-noble. NOTE for the next calibration pass: the same run showed several rows now far looser than the machine they gate - firstPageMs 1204 vs 1800, fullyInteractiveMs 1423 vs 2300, mainThreadBlockDuringOpenMs 91 vs 130, saveMs 1133 vs 1200 and pdfExportMs 3390 vs its 12000 dev-machine projection (the row its own note asks a quiet container run to replace). Those are all safe-direction, so they were left alone here rather than tightened off a single run, but a loose row is a regression that lands unseen.
_comment_findFirstMatchMs: Not a SPEC-047 budget row: this one belongs to SPEC-017's AC-30 ("searching a 200-page document returns first results within 300 ms"), which lives in e2e/SPEC-017.spec.ts and reads only this key. It shares this file because container calibration belongs in one place; SPEC-047's harness iterates its own BUDGETS table and ignores it. Same two-gate shape as the rows above: the spec's 300ms absolute ceiling, plus this baseline +15%. Added 2026-08-17 as a dev-machine projection, not a container measurement — quiet Mac medians of 5 samples were 29-31ms, the same file run alongside five sibling spec files (753% CPU) measured 42ms, so 30 * 1.24 (container) * 1.4 (in-suite contention) ~= 52ms, padded to 80 to leave room for the host-level contention SPEC-047's header describes. A real regression trips the relative gate at 92ms long before the 300ms ceiling; a first QUIET container run should tighten this row.
_comment_pdfExportMs: Not a SPEC-047 budget-table row either: pdfExportMs covers "Export -> PDF (.pdf)" end to end (realize every page, extract each one, load the faces, build the file). Added 2026-09-05 because PDF export is the one path that deliberately turns virtualization OFF — usePrintPreview's realizeAllPages forces all ~256 pages of this fixture into the DOM at once, so the architecture every row above validates does not cover it, and nothing measured it. Like findFirstMatchMs this is a DEV-MACHINE PROJECTION, not a container measurement: a quiet Mac run of this exact flow on this fixture measured 4349ms (256 pages, producing a 44.95 MB PDF). 4349 * 2 (the container runs 2-3x slower on realize/layout-heavy work, as the open path does) * 1.4 (in-suite contention) ~= 12200, so 12000 is that projection rounded down a little. The absolute ceiling is 20000, which leaves the relative gate (12000 * 1.15 = 13800) as the binding one so a real regression trips first. A first QUIET container run should replace this row with a real median of 5. Note that realizeAllPages gives up after 8s with "the document took too long to prepare": if this row ever fails by TIMING OUT rather than by being slow, that deadline is the cause, not the budget.
